title: Split Housing Selector
description: Eight illustrative centrifugal fan situations, one at a time. The learner commits a recommendation (horizontal, three-way, Mohawk pie, standard pie or no split), then picks one of four FanPedia justifications; a situation counts only when both match. One attempt each, mastery 6 of 8, and a summary table of every answer beside the correct one.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Choosing a split housing for a centrifugal fan
learningObjectives: The learner will recommend a horizontal, three-way, Mohawk pie, standard pie or no split housing for eight described centrifugal fan situations, justifying each choice with a FanPedia rule.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); verdicts announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed feedback borders pair with colour; the locked recommendation and the chosen reason show a ✓ prefix and bold outline (aria-pressed). Keys 1-5 choose the split, A-D the reason, Enter goes to the next situation; focus moves to the reason buttons after a split is locked and to Next after a reason.

controls.label: Horizontal / Three-way / Pie, Mohawk / Pie, standard / No split

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Clear every answer and the score and return to situation 1

rules: One recommendation (locked) and one justification per situation; a situation counts correct only when both match the table.

Justification options for situation n: its own justification plus those of the next three rows after n (wrapping past row 8 to row 1) whose recommendation differs from row n's, shown in shuffled order.
Situations 3, 4, 5 and 7 all involve a pie split; the style is decided only by the facts in each situation text.
8 situations in fixed order, one attempt each; running count 'Situations correct: n of 8'; mastery 6 of 8 on the first attempt.
limitations: Covers the three FanPedia split types for centrifugal fans only; gasketing and centering-plate details for leak-tight splits are in Chapter 21.

sources: FanPedia pp. 156-157 and 194: split housing types, Mohawk and standard styles, size 807, three-way drafting time
FanPedia pp. 164 and 168: Arrangements 3SI, 7SI and 7DI include a pie split
FanPedia p. 120: split housings not recommended for nominally leak-tight construction

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit a recommendation, then defend it by choosing the rule that supports it; feedback separates a wrong split from a right split with the wrong reason.
keyQuestions: Does the situation need shipping in sections, passage through an opening, or impeller removal?
Which facts rule out the Mohawk pie split?
When should no split be offered at all?
commonMisconceptions: Any split will let the impeller out without touching the ductwork.
The Mohawk pie split works on any fan.
Adding a split is always harmless.
A horizontal split is only for maintenance, never shipping.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 8'; mastery is 6 of 8 situations with both the recommendation and the justification correct.
